title: A test drives lint.py's deleted-article exemption in a git sandbox
goal: a suite test git-inits a sandbox, commits an article, removes it, and asserts lint.py exits 0 for the removed article's path while a path that never existed exits 1, so the history branch of lint.py refused() that a landing deleting an article depends on is exercised
notes: Found by the SP-wjp5qllo review (S3): BG-eaen55lf's refused() (.claude/skills/kb-verify/lint.py:221) exempts only a deleted path with git history, but the lint sandbox in test_live_kb.py (~line 113) is not a git repo, so the branch never runs; bl_land.changed_articles passes deleted articles, so a broken exemption would stop a landing that deletes one. Also seen: lint.py kb/_self and a kb/_self/backlog/*.json argument exit 0 with errors=0 warnings=0 and lint nothing (within the stated exemption).
